title: Fuel costs and your earnings: seven habits that help
excerpt: You cannot control the pump price. You can control how much fuel each trip burns.
body:
## Why this matters

Fuel is one of the largest costs a driver carries, and prices have been a major reason ride-hailing drivers in Nigeria have protested about fares this year. These habits will not fix prices, but they help.

## Seven habits

- **Drive smoothly.** Gentle acceleration and braking use less fuel.
- **Check tyre pressure weekly.** Soft tyres cost more fuel.
- **Service on time.** A blocked filter or old plugs waste fuel.
- **Remove extra weight.** Empty the boot of things you do not need.
- **Do not idle.** Switch off at long stops where it is safe.
- **Plan your day.** Group trips by area so you drive fewer empty kilometres.
- **Track your costs.** Write down fuel, servicing and data each week so you know your real earnings.

## What each habit does in practice

Smooth driving matters most in Lagos stop and go traffic. Every hard brake wastes the energy you spent speeding up. Look further ahead, ease off early and let the car roll. Tyre pressure and servicing are boring, but they are the cheapest savings you will find. Planning your day matters because empty kilometres cost fuel and pay nothing. If you finish a trip in one area, accept the next request near you rather than driving across town.

## A weekly money check

On the same day each week, write down four numbers: what you earned, what you spent on fuel, what you spent on servicing and what you spent on data. Subtract the costs from the earnings. That is your real income. If the number is lower than you expected, look for the biggest cost first.

## Know your numbers

Your earnings per trip are in the driver app. Compare them with your weekly costs.
